item.title: COVID-19 Under the Microscope: Endothelium in the Spotlight
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor This overview of the cardiovascular dimensions of COVID-19 highlights how far our understanding has evolved since the early reports of myocardial injury in Wuhan. item.title: Re: Medical schools: What’s happening with the planned expansion of places in England?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Alison Moore’s report on the stalled expansion of medical school places, hits a nerve for those of us currently in the system. Whilst politicians debate the ‘15,000’ target, they ignore the reality on the ground, that we are already tripping over each other. For students, this ‘stalled’ progress may feel less like a crisis and more like a reprieve. item.title: Why some patients may feel safer with AI than with clinicians
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear EDitor The BMJ article rightly highlights that AI-assisted disclosure may support earlier detection and shared decision making, particularly when patients feel unable to verbalise distressing material in time-pressured, high-stakes consultations. item.title: Re: Cancer is a chronic disease: why don’t we treat it as one?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor We were delighted to see Adam et al [1] arguing that cancer survivorship care should be part of routine chronic disease management in primary care. Survivors of bone and soft tissue sarcoma have a chronic disease state. Many have been treated as children and most have had surgery for tumour removal. Some have had amputations. item.title: Vitamin D supplementation before IVF in PCOS: limited effect despite severe deficiency — implications for high-risk populations
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor The recent multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial by Zhang et al. evaluated vitamin D supplementation prior to in vitro fertilisation (IVF) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). item.title: Re: Wes Streeting’s links to private health and tech companies under fire in wake of Mandelson texts
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, 'Streeting said the donation was “towards staffing costs in my constituency office.”' He should be expected to provide a breakdown; this sounds like a universal get-out-of-jail-card. More transparency is needed: after all, we cannot accept as little as a Post-It note, some of which would have been very acceptable in my Secretary's office...
